projects.name: Voice agents on ElevenLabs, with an MCP tool server
projects.oneLine: Seconds before a call ends, my dental agent calls a tool on my MCP server that writes the call’s state to the database, so the dental app shows it before the caller hangs up.

families.name: Interview agents
families.text: A technical-role interviewer and a functional (business-role) interviewer. About 10 to 15 real candidate interviews run.

families.name: Dental front-desk agents
families.text: Inbound and outbound calls: schedule, cancel and reschedule appointments; answer questions about providers, doctors and general website enquiries; lead conversion and lead management for dental patients.

families.name: Insurance-verification agent
families.text: Speaks with insurance-provider representatives to collect the dental codes the existing RPA bot flow misses, and writes them to the database through MCP. Paired with the existing application by database polling on call creation, so the existing flow was not broken.

built: 15 ElevenLabs voice agents across two workspaces, in three families; 10 have logged usage.
Branching workflows of 9 to 10 nodes, with the LLM for each node chosen by task difficulty; up to about 50 versions on one agent.

The MCP-over-SSE tool server, built alone (91 of 113 commits): Bun and Express with a React front end, 11 SQL-backed tools (patients, appointments, availability, eligibility), on Azure App Service, shared by agents in two workspaces.
Multi-provider LLM orchestration across Groq, Azure OpenAI and Gemini, with live failover under rate limits.
Multilingual support with knowledge attached to the model; graceful and abrupt call endings handled.
checked: Test-driven development, a bug tracker and ordered SQL migrations on the tool server.
I read waterfall traces in Arize Phoenix to debug the agents.
I adapted the agents to ElevenLabs feature releases as they shipped, by trial and error.
notClaimed: The phone lines and call services were built by other teams; I use them.
The insurance-verification agent is not live.

projects.name: cluBITSTranslator
projects.oneLine: A Dockerized FastAPI service that translates PDF, DOCX, XLSX and PPTX files and keeps their layout. Taken to a priced proposal.
built: Per-format pipelines: OOXML text-node patching for Word and PowerPoint, openpyxl for Excel, font-fitted re-rendering with a QA validator for PDF.
OpenRouter vision models for OCR, a translation cache, per-job cost tracking, Azure Blob, MSSQL telemetry and crash recovery.
checked: Taken to a priced commercial proposal: a hybrid of Azure Translator, Google Translate and a custom LLM under one subscription, positioned on price, OCR, analytics, India data residency and on-premise deployment.
notClaimed: The client is not named, and no usage volume is claimed.

projects.name: SafeSupport
projects.oneLine: A support-triage agent over real customer-support conversations, with an evaluation harness. Bulk labels wait for human sign-off.
built: Intent classification, a retrieval-grounded draft reply, and a decision to auto-handle or escalate.
An evaluation harness with baselines and ablations; 123 passing tests.
checked: In data prep I rejected mid-thread fragments: 24,253 of 106,860 brand replies, about 23%.
Bulk labelling waits for explicit human sign-off, because golden labels cannot come from the model class being evaluated.
notClaimed: No accuracy figure is quoted here; the evaluation is in the repo.
